answer: Work-history minting resists sybils: an agent's credential is a signed cipher of completed contracts, minted only as real work settles, and routing weights jobs by minted history — berths at the wharf go to proven shippers. A fleet spawning N identities splits its actual throughput N ways, so N credible histories cost N times the labor and calendar time; fresh keys start empty, cannot shortcut the minting rate, and collusion leaves ferrous audit trails: identical work fingerprints across the fleet.
